title: Controlled reopening of developmental critical periods

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a controlled, temporary return of developmental brain plasticity: making an established circuit sufficiently adaptable for appropriate experience or rehabilitation to rebuild its function, then restoring the stability needed to preserve that recovery. The clearest demonstration case is amblyopia in older children and adults, where reduced plasticity limits the effectiveness of delayed treatment. The intended result is durable recovery of normal-range visual acuity and binocular function beyond the usual developmental treatment window.

A biological basis comes from molecular constraints on mature circuits. In mouse visual cortex, Lynx1 limits plasticity through its influence on nicotinic acetylcholine receptor signaling and helps maintain mature network stability. Removing this constraint has enabled adult mouse visual recovery. The proposed human capability combines several further requirements: targeting the relevant circuit, limiting the period of increased plasticity, guiding useful rebuilding, and subsequently restoring stability. The supplied studies do not demonstrate that combined capability.

significance.text: Durable normalization of amblyopic vision after the usual developmental window would create a major restorative capability. It could allow older children and adults to recover functions that delayed treatment often improves less effectively. Its significance would rest on meaningful recovery of both the affected eye and coordinated binocular vision, extending beyond small improvements on an acuity chart. This is a conditional assessment of the proposed achievement, not a prediction that existing interventions will produce it.

The central scientific opportunity is to control the balance between adaptability and stability. The mouse Lynx1 findings suggest that some restrictions on adult visual plasticity are actively maintained and can be experimentally altered. They do not establish that a mature human brain can safely be returned to a juvenile state, or that reopening plasticity alone reconstructs normal perception. The therapeutic aim would be enough targeted adaptability to support recovery, followed by reliable preservation of the rebuilt function.

Conditional extension: successful control of developmental plasticity might also support recovery of selected language or motor deficits. Each application would require separate evidence that the relevant mechanisms can be controlled, sufficient circuitry remains recoverable, effective training can guide rebuilding, and the resulting function can be stabilized safely. Shared molecular brakes alone would not make recovery follow, and the supplied evidence does not establish broad claims that early language or motor deficits are generally reversible.

missing_breakthrough.text: The proposed missing capability is selective, reversible control of human circuit plasticity that produces substantial functional recovery and then restores stability. The mouse Lynx1 work establishes an experimentally manipulable constraint, but recovery in knockout animals does not demonstrate a time-limited therapeutic release followed by deliberate reclosure. A human intervention would need control over where, when, and how strongly plasticity changes.

Target specificity remains a concrete mechanistic barrier. The 2026 mouse study used broad histone-deacetylase inhibition, affecting multiple HDAC isoforms. Its reported reduction in HDAC3 was associated with the observed changes but did not establish HDAC3 as their causal driver. Identifying which targets produce useful plasticity, and separating those effects from broader drug actions, remains necessary before these findings can justify a selective treatment mechanism.

Functional rebuilding is a separate challenge from increasing plasticity. The human donepezil pilot reported modest acuity gains without significant group-level improvement in stereoacuity. Its uncontrolled design, together with concurrent patching in minors, leaves treatment attribution unresolved. Establishing a useful intervention therefore requires showing that the treatment and accompanying experience cause meaningful recovery across the intended functions, rather than assuming that a plasticity-related mechanism or an acuity gain demonstrates complete circuit repair.

Engineering synthesis: the intervention must also stop creating vulnerability once rehabilitation ends. Durable performance after treatment withdrawal would be necessary but would not, by itself, establish restored resistance to maladaptive plasticity or circuit selectivity. Concrete development problems include defining the treatment window, choosing effective training, measuring effects outside the intended circuit, and detecting lasting cognitive or psychiatric harm. These are proposed requirements for the combined capability, not properties already established by the supplied studies.

current_state.text: Morishita, Miwa, Heintz, and Hensch reported in Science on 26 November 2010 that Lynx1 expression increases after the mouse visual critical period and that its removal enhances nicotinic acetylcholine receptor signaling. The figure captions retained in the supplied review describe adult Lynx1-knockout mice recovering visual-evoked-potential acuity to normal levels after a previously deprived eye was reopened. This supports adult mouse recovery on an electrophysiological acuity measure; it does not establish comprehensive normal perception or a reversible treatment. The reviewed material was a PubMed abstract and figure captions, without inspection of the full paper or figure images.

Wu, Hensch, and colleagues reported an open-label pilot in Scientific Reports on 22 June 2023 involving 16 participants aged 9–37 years prescribed 12 weeks of donepezil. Participants under 18 also received patching. The abstract reports a mean amblyopic-eye acuity improvement of 1.2 lines, with a range of 0.0–3.0 lines; 4 of 16 participants, or 25%, improved by at least two lines. The review notes that the Results section describes a median 1.2-line gain, leaving the mean-versus-median reporting difference unresolved.

The donepezil study reported persistence of gains approximately 10 weeks after treatment stopped, with the primary outcome assessed at 22 weeks. Stereoacuity did not show significant group-level improvement. The small sample, absence of a placebo group, and patching in minors limit causal attribution and do not establish normal human vision or controlled reopening and restabilization of a critical period. The supplied review covered the full main article, but supplementary material and figure images were not inspected.

Ding and colleagues reported in Neuroscience Letters in 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.neulet.2026.138548, that broad HDAC inhibition with trichostatin A improved synaptic-plasticity-related measures in adult amblyopic mice. The reviewed abstract describes findings involving synaptic ultrastructure, VGLUT2, and long-term potentiation. Because the inhibitor affects multiple HDAC isoforms, the associated reduction in HDAC3 does not establish a causal role for that specific target. The supplied review had access to the PubMed abstract rather than the full experimental report; these findings do not establish normal human vision.

Evidence-bounded synthesis: the supplied record demonstrates manipulation of adult mouse visual plasticity and preliminary, uncontrolled human acuity gains. It does not demonstrate the proposed combination of selective human reopening, normal-range functional rebuilding, and safe restabilization, or its extension to language or motor systems. No bounded freshness search was supplied, so these dated studies cannot establish the complete state of the field or the field-wide absence of such capabilities as of 1 November 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed visual demonstration: conduct a randomized, placebo-controlled trial in people beyond the classical visual critical period, pairing a time-limited intervention with appropriate visual experience or rehabilitation. Prespecify age-appropriate normal ranges for amblyopic-eye acuity and binocular function, and require most participants to reach those ranges. Training and patching should be controlled sufficiently to identify the intervention's contribution. These are proposed completion thresholds, not published consensus standards; a one-line chart improvement would not meet this proposal.
completion_criteria.label: Most participants beyond critical period attain normal-range acuity and binocularity

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and control demonstration: retain the functional gains during prespecified follow-up after treatment withdrawal, while separately assessing circuit selectivity and restored resistance to maladaptive plasticity. Use a defined cognitive and psychiatric assessment plan with sufficiently long follow-up to detect lasting harm. Persistence after withdrawal is already an outcome considered in the donepezil pilot, but durability alone would not establish all the control and safety properties proposed here.
completion_criteria.label: Post-withdrawal gains persist with circuit selectivity, restored stability, and safety

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independently reproduce the findings and report response distributions, nonresponders, adverse effects, treatment burden, and variation by age, deficit severity, and prior treatment. Establish the usable intervention and training window rather than assuming one protocol applies across patients. A second demonstration could test the same principle in a non-visual system, such as motor recovery after early injury in school-age children. Success would establish demonstrated breadth across the tested settings, not universal reopening of developmental critical periods.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication reports patient outcomes and usable intervention and training windows

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison with PED-05, Prevention of cerebral palsy after perinatal brain injury: both concern developmental brain function and could involve overlapping rehabilitation needs. PED-04 centers on rebuilding function by controlling plasticity after a developmental window, whereas PED-05's title centers on preventing cerebral palsy following perinatal injury. The research frames the latter contrast as acute protection or repair, but the supplied roster contains no detailed PED-05 description to verify its precise timing or mechanisms. The concepts remain distinct and could potentially combine.

Roster-based comparison with PED-09, Post-symptomatic restoration of severe genetic neurodevelopmental disorders: both seek recovery after a developmental deficit has appeared. PED-04 concerns control of circuit adaptability and subsequent stability; PED-09 is defined by severe genetic disorders and post-symptomatic restoration. The research contrasts plasticity control with restoring a missing gene product, but PED-09's supplied title does not establish that all its approaches involve gene-product replacement. Correcting an underlying molecular defect and enabling circuit relearning could be complementary requirements.

Roster-based comparison with PED-08, Restoration of nephron endowment after the nephrogenic clock stops: both address a capability constrained by developmental timing. Their biological endpoints differ: PED-04 seeks functional reorganization of neural circuits, while PED-08 seeks restoration of nephron endowment. The timing analogy does not imply shared mechanisms or that evidence of neural plasticity supports restarting kidney development.

Roster-based comparison with PED-03, Reversal of established childhood stunting and its cognitive cost: the potential overlap is recovery of developmental cognitive consequences after a deficit is established. PED-04 supplies a proposed circuit-plasticity strategy, while PED-03 describes a broader growth and cognitive-restoration goal. The supplied material does not establish that reopening critical periods would reverse the cognitive effects associated with stunting.

change_log.reason: These combined requirements distinguish the proposed innovation from a general increase in plasticity or a modest treatment response.

change_log.change: Restricted the Lynx1 mechanism to demonstrated mouse visual-cortex evidence and specified normal visual-evoked-potential acuity as the reported recovery endpoint.
change_log.reason: The supplied abstract and captions do not establish comprehensive normal perception, a reversible intervention, or human efficacy.

change_log.change: Added concurrent patching in minors, lack of significant group-level stereoacuity improvement, approximately 10-week post-treatment persistence, and the mean-versus-median discrepancy to the donepezil account.
change_log.reason: These details materially affect attribution, functional scope, durability, and interpretation of the quantitative result.

change_log.change: Specified the 2026 study's broad HDAC inhibition and synaptic endpoints, while distinguishing HDAC3 association from causation.
change_log.reason: The reviewed abstract supports plasticity-related mouse findings without establishing a selective causal target.

change_log.change: Replaced categorical field-wide absence claims with conclusions bounded by the supplied studies and acknowledged the missing freshness assessment.
change_log.reason: The evidence does not demonstrate the combined human capability, but it cannot establish its absence throughout the field as of November 2026.

change_log.change: Qualified language and motor applications and removed broad assertions about rehabilitation rarely erasing early deficits.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence supports the visual rationale; cross-system recovery requires additional mechanisms, recoverable circuitry, effective training, and safety evidence.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria to include prespecified normal ranges, selectivity, restabilization, defined safety follow-up, independent reproduction, and practical response boundaries.
change_log.reason: Acuity gains and persistence alone would not demonstrate the full proposed capability. The thresholds remain explicitly proposed.

change_log.change: Retained source-access limitations and qualified related-concept comparisons using the available roster titles.
change_log.reason: The review did not inspect all full papers, images, or supplements, and detailed definitions of the neighboring innovations were not supplied.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record contains no bounded freshness assessment establishing the complete field state as of 1 November 2026.
The donepezil article's abstract reports a mean 1.2-line gain, while the reviewed Results text describes a median 1.2-line gain; the discrepancy remains unresolved.
The human pilot cannot separate donepezil's contribution from other influences, including concurrent patching in minors, and does not establish normal binocular function.
The supplied evidence does not establish selective, reversible human plasticity control or safe restoration of circuit stability after reopening.
The causal contribution of HDAC3 to the 2026 mouse findings remains unresolved because trichostatin A inhibits multiple HDAC isoforms.
Exact normal-range definitions, follow-up duration, selectivity measures, and acceptable safety boundaries for the proposed demonstrations remain to be specified.
Language and motor generalization, including the recoverability of affected circuits, requires separate evidence.
The 2010 and 2026 mouse reports were reviewed through partial PubMed material; the 2023 article's supplementary material and figure images were not inspected.
Precise mechanistic and timing boundaries for PED-05 and PED-09 cannot be verified from roster titles alone.

brief.title: Restoring the brain’s early capacity to rebuild
possible: Older children and adults with amblyopia, reduced vision caused by abnormal visual input early in life, could regain normal visual sharpness and coordinated use of both eyes. Treatment would briefly restore the brain’s ability to adapt, guide recovery through visual experience, then stabilize the rebuilt connections.
why: People who missed the usual childhood treatment window would gain another chance at lasting recovery. The benefit would extend beyond reading smaller letters on a chart to recovering how the eyes work together.

sources.who: Hirofumi Morishita, Julie M Miwa, Nathaniel Heintz and Takao K Hensch
sources.showed: Removing Lynx1, a protein that limits brain adaptability, allowed adult mice to recover normal visual sharpness measured through electrical brain responses after a deprived eye reopened.
sources.quote: Here, we identified an increase in expression of Lynx1 protein in mice that prevented plasticity in the primary visual cortex late in life.
sources.cited_for: Molecular constraints on adaptability in the adult brain can be altered to support visual recovery.
sources.not_established: Permanently removing a protein does not establish a temporary treatment that restores stability afterward.

sources.showed: A small human study of the drug donepezil found modest gains in visual sharpness. It lacked a placebo group, and children also wore eye patches. Depth perception did not significantly improve across the group.
sources.quote: Gains were maintained 10 weeks after cessation of donepezil and were similar for children and adults.
sources.cited_for: Some human visual gains persisted after treatment stopped.
sources.not_established: The study cannot establish that donepezil caused the gains or restored normal coordinated vision.

sources.showed: An enriched environment (EE) and trichostatin A, a drug affecting several enzymes, improved measures of adaptability at connections between brain cells in adult amblyopic mice. Changes accompanied lower levels of the enzyme HDAC3.
sources.quote: Our findings revealed that EE enhanced synaptic plasticity in visual cortex of adult amblyopia mice and was associated with reduced HDAC3 expression.
sources.cited_for: Adult mouse visual circuits retain experimentally alterable mechanisms of adaptability.
sources.not_established: The findings do not establish that HDAC3 caused the changes or that the treatment restores normal human vision.

shown: Morishita and colleagues restored normal visual sharpness on an electrical brain measure in adult mice lacking a molecular brake. Wu and colleagues reported modest, lasting human gains in a small uncontrolled drug study. Neither demonstrated temporary, targeted reopening followed by restored stability.
missing: A human treatment must temporarily increase adaptability in the intended brain circuit with control over its timing and strength.
Treatment and guided experience must cause normal visual sharpness and coordinated use of both eyes beyond the usual childhood window.
Recovery must survive treatment withdrawal, with restored resistance to harmful changes and no lasting cognitive or psychiatric harm.

milestones.label: Most older patients regain normal sharpness and coordinated vision
milestones.explanation: A randomized trial against an inactive treatment would need most participants to reach defined normal ranges for sharpness and coordinated vision, with training controlled. This would establish recovery beyond the usual window.

milestones.label: Recovery lasts with targeted effects, restored stability and safety
milestones.explanation: Follow-up after treatment stops would need lasting gains, effects confined to intended circuits, resistance to harmful changes, and cognitive and psychiatric safety. This would establish control beyond temporary improvement.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce recovery and define usable treatment windows
milestones.explanation: Independent studies would need to reproduce recovery, report who benefits, harms and burden, and define treatment and training windows across patient groups. This would establish reproducibility and practical limits.

uncertain: The normal ranges, follow-up duration and acceptable boundaries for targeting and safety remain to be defined.
It remains unclear which molecular targets cause useful adaptability rather than accompanying broader drug effects.
Recovery of language or movement would require separate demonstrations that the relevant circuits can rebuild and stabilize.

page.title: Reversible reopening of visual critical-period plasticity
page.definition: In adults with amblyopia, a lasting loss of vision caused by abnormal visual experience early in life, a treatment would temporarily make selected circuits in the visual cortex more responsive to visual input. During this window, the affected eye would recover acuity, the ability to resolve fine detail, and the two eyes would recover stereopsis, the ability to judge depth from differences between their images. Both gains would persist after the circuits return to their usual adult level of plasticity.

goal.need: In a Rotterdam cohort, the estimated lifetime risk of vision worse than 20/40 in both eyes was 18% with amblyopia and 10% without it. Even after glasses bring an image into focus, the brain can still favour the stronger eye. Patching encourages use of the weaker eye, but treatment usually works less well in adults. Renewed sensitivity to input from both eyes could help adults see finer detail and judge depth more precisely. The input matters: in mice, closing one eye during a reopened window reduced acuity through that eye.

figures.caption: Response to additional amblyopia treatment
figures.note: Responders gained at least 10 letters, equivalent to two chart lines, by 24 weeks. Additional treatment comprised patching and near activities; children aged 7–12 years also received atropine.

statements.quote: allow some recovery of visual function and stereopsis in adult amblyopia subjects.
statements.context: The fiscal year 2021 Congressional Justification describes research directed at opening the critical period.

statements.quote: Manipulate extracellular matrix factors and immune cells in perineuronal nets (PNN) as potential therapeutic approaches to modulate plasticity.
statements.context: The plan links the formation of these nets around neurons in visual cortex to closure of the critical period. It names a therapeutic approach without prescribing a human recovery endpoint.

completion.title: Adults recover amblyopic vision through targeted reopening followed by reclosure of visual plasticity.
completion.criterion: A controlled human study demonstrates that a temporary intervention increases experience-dependent plasticity in the intended visual circuit, improves amblyopic-eye acuity and stereopsis beyond matched rehabilitation alone, and then restores the circuit's pretreatment adult plasticity while those visual gains persist. Reopening, spatial confinement and reclosure require measurements distinct from the visual recovery endpoints.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no outside body was found to define the integrated human capability.
completion.basis: Searches of NEI goals, DARPA SHINE criteria, FDA pages, AAO material and registered amblyopia endpoints found no published test for integrated human reopening, reclosure and visual recovery. This fallback combines the NEI's adult visual-recovery goal with DARPA's spatial and temporal control goal. No population-response fraction, normal-vision cutoff or fixed follow-up interval is assigned.

milestones.title: Adult amblyopic mice recover cortical visual acuity to undeprived values.
milestones.criterion: Close one eye from postnatal day 19 to day 33 in wild-type mice, then reopen it for more than one month. Begin daily physostigmine on day 45. After day 60, estimate acuity through the previously deprived eye from visual evoked potentials in primary visual cortex, in cycles per degree. Test for higher acuity than with eye reopening alone and compare the recovered value with acuity in treated, undeprived wild-type mice. The assay specifies no equivalence margin.
milestones.set_by: Morishita et al., Science, published mouse amblyopia-recovery protocol and Figure 3; an experimental endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: reopening the deprived eye together with cholinesterase inhibitor restores vision

milestones.title: Adult mouse visual plasticity reopens transiently and resists brief deprivation after an 18-day washout.
milestones.criterion: In adult wild-type mice, assess cortical acuity from visual evoked potentials after four days of monocular deprivation. Deprivation must reduce acuity during seven days of RK-peptide infusion into visual cortex and at the seven-day washout, with resistance to the same deprivation at the 18-day washout. Use saline and control peptides to test whether the change in susceptibility is specific to RK peptide.
milestones.set_by: Beurdeley et al., adult-mouse monocular deprivation assay, Figure 7.
milestones.threshold_quote: A brief window of plasticity persists <18 d after RK peptide treatment ends.

milestones.title: A week-22 responder with residual amblyopia retains a gain of at least 15 letters after treatment.
milestones.criterion: For participants aged eight years or older with residual amblyopia, compare best-corrected acuity in the amblyopic eye at baseline and week 22, ten weeks after the 12-week treatment course ends. Report the number and proportion gaining at least 15 letters, equivalent to three chart lines. The registry defines an individual response without setting a minimum proportion that must respond.
milestones.set_by: Carolyn Wu and Boston Children's Hospital, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01584076, primary outcome measure.
milestones.threshold_quote: ≥ 15 letters or 3 logMAR lines at 22 weeks after 10 weeks off study treatment.

milestones.title: An intervention achieves at least a 3:1 target-to-off-target selectivity ratio for brain plasticity.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate a target-to-off-target intervention selectivity ratio of at least 3:1 at the site of intended neuroplasticity. If stimulation acts through a projection to a different brain region, measure the resulting biological effect at the intended downstream target and compare it with the effect in nontarget tissue.
milestones.set_by: DARPA SHINE Disruption Opportunity and programme overview, intervention selectivity metric. FAQ 27 specifies the measurement site.

milestones.title: An adult amblyopia trial shows an acuity benefit over placebo at 10 weeks that persists at 22 weeks.
milestones.criterion: Randomize adults to active treatment or placebo with matched optical correction, patching and visual training. Use the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study letter chart to measure change from baseline in amblyopic-eye acuity. The mean gain must favour active treatment at week 10 in the primary comparison and at week 22 in the secondary follow-up comparison. Use the published repeated-measures analysis of covariance and P < 0.05 for the between-group comparisons.
milestones.set_by: Hermo Pharma Ltd, EudraCT 2010-023216-14, sections E.5.1–E.5.2; statistical criterion in Huttunen et al.'s published analysis. These are protocol-specific efficacy and follow-up endpoints.
milestones.threshold_quote: Change from baseline (Week 0) to end of follow-up (Week 22) in visual acuity in the amblyopic eye

milestones.title: A targeted intervention reopens visual plasticity in adults and then restores its pretreatment level.
milestones.criterion: In adults, demonstrate increased experience-dependent plasticity in the intended visual circuit during intervention and return to its pretreatment adult level after intervention ends, with measurements in nontarget circuits. Acuity improvement or persistence alone does not meet this mechanistic test. This establishes temporal control before requiring retained acuity and stereopsis recovery from the same intervention.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: searches of NEI goals, DARPA criteria and registered amblyopia endpoints found no validated human reopening/reclosure test or numerical cutoff.

milestones.title: Brief closure of one eye reduces cortical binocularity in cats beyond the susceptible period.
milestones.criterion: In cats beyond the period normally sensitive to brief closure of one eye, record responses of individual visual cortical neurons to stimulation of each eye. During local norepinephrine perfusion, eye closure must reduce the proportion of neurons driven by both eyes in the perfused region. Compare nearby cortex in the same animal and perfusion during normal binocular vision.
milestones.set_by: Kasamatsu, Pettigrew and Ary, published cortical perfusion and monocular deprivation assay.
milestones.threshold_quote: in the older animals a decrease in binocularity was obtained.

milestones.title: Adults with anisometropic amblyopia retain improved stereoacuity one year after training.
milestones.criterion: In adults whose amblyopia arose from unequal refractive errors, measure the smallest binocular disparity they can discriminate before and after six two-hour sessions over four weeks and again at one month, three months and one year. Use the TNO stereotest, with the Lang stereotest for coarse stereopsis as in the published protocol. A retained gain requires a lower stereoacuity threshold than at baseline at the one-year visit in participants who improved during training.
milestones.set_by: Lunghi et al., adult anisometropic amblyopia training protocol and one-year stereoacuity follow-up, Figure 3B.
milestones.threshold_quote: 1 month, 3 months, and 1 year after the end of the training.

not_found: Group sizes for Beurdeley et al.'s RK-peptide washout comparison could not be verified.
Ding et al.'s full report could not be opened; its abstract does not give sample sizes.
The full 2024 fluoxetine report could not be opened, so its post-withdrawal results could not be verified.

results.finding: Among 55 adults with amblyopia, fluoxetine produced a greater three-month acuity gain than placebo (P = 0.04).
results.detail: Both groups continued patching. The study reports outcomes after three months, but does not report the specified week-10 endpoint or week-22 withdrawal follow-up.
results.quote: The mean logMAR visual acuity of the amblyopic eye improved by 0.20 ± 0.24 (0-0.8) in the fluoxetine group (P < 0.001) and by 0.08 ± 0.15 (0-0.7) in the placebo group (P = 0.01); mean logMAR improvement was significantly higher in the fluoxetine group than in the placebo group (P = 0.04).

results.finding: Adult wild-type mice given cholinesterase inhibitor after deprivation (n = 4) recovered V1 acuity to 0.48 cycles/degree.
results.quote: In contrast, reopening the deprived eye together with cholinesterase inhibitor restores vision (grey bar, AChEI: 0.48 ± 0.06 cyc/deg, 4 mice; vs WT + eye open, * P < 0.05; vs WT no MD + AChEI: 0.47 ± 0.02 cyc/deg, 6mice, P > 0.8, t-test).

results.finding: Adult Lynx1 knockout mice given focal diazepam during monocular deprivation (n = 6) had a contralateral bias index of 0.67.
results.quote: Focal diazepam infusion during adult MD in lynx1 KO mice abolishes ocular dominance plasticity (black, DZ: CBI = 0.67, 6 mice vs grey, vehicle: CBI = 0.54, 14 mice; *** P < 0.001, t-test).

results.finding: In 16 participants with residual amblyopia, median best-corrected amblyopic-eye acuity improved by 1.0 line at week 22.
results.detail: The paper reports a maximum gain of 3.0 lines without explicitly assigning it to week 22.
results.quote: This improvement was sustained at the final outcome visit at 22 weeks, 10 weeks after stopping treatment (median improvement 1.0 lines (97.87% CI 0.6–1.8)).

results.finding: Five adults with residual amblyopia had a median amblyopic-eye acuity gain of 1.2 E-ETDRS lines at week 12 on donepezil.
results.detail: The numerical week-22 gain reported in the text pools the five adults and 11 younger participants.

results.finding: In adult amblyopic mice (n unreported), trichostatin A potentiated visual cortical long-term potentiation. The effect size was unreported.
results.detail: Trichostatin A inhibits multiple histone deacetylase isoforms. The reduction in HDAC3 expression was correlational.
results.quote: Similarly, the broad HDAC inhibitor TSA, improved synaptic ultrastructure, increased VGLUT2 expression, and potentiated LTP, functionally resembling several key effects of EE.

results.finding: Among 34 adults with amblyopia assessed at week 22, 15 retained a gain of at least 10 ETDRS letters.
results.detail: Patching and training ended at week 10. The methods describe a two-week medication taper, while the results describe week 22 as 12 weeks after treatment discontinuation.

results.finding: In 42 randomized adults with amblyopia, the week-10 ETDRS acuity difference was 0.027 logMAR in favour of placebo.
results.detail: At week 22, reported mean acuity was 0.474 logMAR with fluoxetine and 0.420 with placebo. The corresponding baseline means were 0.645 and 0.636 logMAR.
results.quote: At the primary endpoint, the mean treatment group difference in visual acuity improvement was only 0.027 logMAR units (95% CI: −0.057 to 0.110; p = 0.524).

results.finding: Adult amblyopic mice (5 per group) showed improved VEP-derived acuity after RK peptide treatment (P < 0.01).

results.finding: Six of 10 adults with anisometropic amblyopia improved their stereoacuity during training and were reported to retain the gain at one year.
results.detail: The text does not give individual one-year thresholds or explicitly count how many of the six responders attended the one-year visit.

definition = "In adults with amblyopia, a lasting loss of vision caused by abnormal visual experience early in life, a treatment would temporarily make selected circuits in the visual cortex more responsive to visual input. During this window, the affected eye would recover acuity, the ability to resolve fine detail, and the two eyes would recover stereopsis, the ability to judge depth from differences between their images. Both gains would persist after the circuits return to their usual adult level of plasticity.". Reason: The definition now distinguishes the temporary change in responsiveness from the lasting change in vision and specifies the binocular cue that defines stereopsis.

goal.need = "In a Rotterdam cohort, the estimated lifetime risk of vision worse than 20/40 in both eyes was 18% with amblyopia and 10% without it. Even after glasses bring an image into focus, the brain can still favour the stronger eye. Patching encourages use of the weaker eye, but treatment usually works less well in adults. Renewed sensitivity to input from both eyes could help adults see finer detail and judge depth more precisely. The input matters: in mice, closing one eye during a reopened window reduced acuity through that eye.". Reason: The adolescent trial alone does not explain the burden adults face, why optical correction can leave a deficit, or what recovering binocular vision would mean for them.

add statement by National Eye Institute, Strategic Plan: Vision for the Future, 2021–2025, 2021: "Manipulate extracellular matrix factors and immune cells in perineuronal nets (PNN) as potential therapeutic approaches to modulate plasticity.". Reason: The strategic plan names a specific therapeutic approach and explains its connection to closure of the visual critical period.

add milestone after None: "Brief closure of one eye reduces cortical binocularity in cats beyond the susceptible period.". Reason: The existing milestones begin with acuity recovery and omit the earlier demonstration that altered visual input can again change cortical responses after the susceptible period.

edit m1: criterion = "Close one eye from postnatal day 19 to day 33 in wild-type mice, then reopen it for more than one month. Begin daily physostigmine on day 45. After day 60, estimate acuity through the previously deprived eye from visual evoked potentials in primary visual cortex, in cycles per degree. Test for higher acuity than with eye reopening alone and compare the recovered value with acuity in treated, undeprived wild-type mice. The assay specifies no equivalence margin."; refs = [5]. Reason: The criterion replaces observed group means and sample sizes with the assay and identifies the treated undeprived controls used in the published comparison.

edit m2: criterion = "In adult wild-type mice, assess cortical acuity from visual evoked potentials after four days of monocular deprivation. Deprivation must reduce acuity during seven days of RK-peptide infusion into visual cortex and at the seven-day washout, with resistance to the same deprivation at the 18-day washout. Use saline and control peptides to test whether the change in susceptibility is specific to RK peptide."; set_by = "Beurdeley et al., adult-mouse monocular deprivation assay, Figure 7."; threshold_quote = "A brief window of plasticity persists <18 d after RK peptide treatment ends."; threshold_ref = 6; refs = [6]. Reason: Figure 7 tests susceptibility to deprivation at seven and 18 days of washout, while the acuity recovery and sample size previously included in the criterion belong to Figure 8.

edit m3: title = "A week-22 responder with residual amblyopia retains a gain of at least 15 letters after treatment."; criterion = "For participants aged eight years or older with residual amblyopia, compare best-corrected acuity in the amblyopic eye at baseline and week 22, ten weeks after the 12-week treatment course ends. Report the number and proportion gaining at least 15 letters, equivalent to three chart lines. The registry defines an individual response without setting a minimum proportion that must respond."; set_by = "Carolyn Wu and Boston Children's Hospital, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01584076, primary outcome measure."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "\u2265 15 letters or 3 logMAR lines at 22 weeks after 10 weeks off study treatment."; threshold_ref = 21; refs = [21, 7]. Reason: The registry defines a 15-letter responder endpoint, which a statistically significant group change or a one-line median gain cannot establish.

edit m4: criterion = "Demonstrate a target-to-off-target intervention selectivity ratio of at least 3:1 at the site of intended neuroplasticity. If stimulation acts through a projection to a different brain region, measure the resulting biological effect at the intended downstream target and compare it with the effect in nontarget tissue."; set_by = "DARPA SHINE Disruption Opportunity and programme overview, intervention selectivity metric. FAQ 27 specifies the measurement site."; threshold_quote = "3:1 Ratio (Target vs.\nOff-Target)"; threshold_ref = 3; refs = [3, 8, 13]. Reason: The programme table supplies the missing ratio quotation, and the FAQ specifies where to measure it for an intervention acting through a neural projection.

edit m5: criterion = "Randomize adults to active treatment or placebo with matched optical correction, patching and visual training. Use the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study letter chart to measure change from baseline in amblyopic-eye acuity. The mean gain must favour active treatment at week 10 in the primary comparison and at week 22 in the secondary follow-up comparison. Use the published repeated-measures analysis of covariance and P < 0.05 for the between-group comparisons."; refs = [4, 10]. Reason: The published analysis specifies a between-group comparison at both visits, which the previous criterion obscured by including outcomes from two different trials.

add milestone after m5: "Adults with anisometropic amblyopia retain improved stereoacuity one year after training.". Reason: The human milestones measure letter acuity, leaving retained stereopsis untested until completion even though an adult protocol measures it directly.
